chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, raised it (to the Imam), saying:

It was said to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), 'You claim that drinking wine is more severe than adultery and theft?' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes. The perpetrator of adultery may not proceed to other sins, but the wine drinker, when he drinks wine, commits adultery, and theft, and kills the soul whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, prohibited, and neglects the Prayer.'
ai.seo_question: Why is drinking wine considered more severe than adultery and theft in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) elucidates the hierarchical severity of wine by describing it as the 'gateway' to all sins, arguing that the wine drinker accumulates the penalties of adultery, theft, murder, and prayer neglect simultaneously. This reflects the Shia scholarly view of *khamr* not merely as a prohibited substance but as a catalyst that dissolves moral restraint, leading to a compounding of spiritual and legal transgressions. The narration underscores the comprehensive nature of wine's impact on both individual piety and communal order.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, raising it, said,

‘It was said to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>, ‘You<sup>asws</sup> are claiming that drinking wine is more severe than the adultery and the theft?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes. The perpetrator of the adultery would perhaps not get invited to something else (from the sins), and the wine drinker, when he drinks the wine, would commit adultery, and theft, and murder the soul whom Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Prohibited, and would neglect the Prayer’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn in a marfu‘ manner has said the following:

“It was said to ’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘You think that drinking wine is a sin which is more serious than fornication and theft.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, because a fornicator perhaps does not extend it to other sins but a wine drinker when he drinks, fornicates, steals and murders a soul which Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has made unlawful to kill, and neglects Salat (prayer).”’
